Summary: Monophysitism taught in the 5th century that Christ has only one nature, in which his humanity was absorbed into his divinity. Eutyches was a leading figure in the controversy.
Beliefs: Christ has one nature only; Christ's humanity was absorbed by his divinity; Christ is not fully human in the same way as other humans
Controversy: Condemned at the Council of Chalcedon AD 451, which defined Christ in two natures without confusion or separation
ChristianResponse: The church affirmed that Jesus is fully God and fully man in one person, citing Hebrews 4:15 and Colossians 2:9.
RelatedDoctrines: Incarnation; Hypostatic Union; Humanity of Christ
